llm.summary: The skill broadly matches its marketing purpose, but there are multiple inconsistencies: hardcoded API keys committed in the repo, undisclosed system dependencies (Chrome/Xvfb) and shell execution, and code that reaches into other skills' filesystem — you should not install/run it without remediation and careful review.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a Node.js-only marketing tool with no required env vars or binaries, but the code expects /usr/bin/google-chrome, uses Xvfb, and can spawn shell commands. It also includes an integration to invoke another local skill's run_render.py. Those capabilities (browser automation, launching system services, calling other skills) are not reflected in the description or the declared requirements.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs cloning the GitHub repo and configuring API keys (normal), but the runtime instructions/code will: launch Chrome (execSync), attempt to start Xvfb, perform headless scraping of douyin.com (via system chrome), call external APIs (api.deepseek.com / api.tikhub.io) and call a script in ~/.openclaw-agent2 workspace if present. The agent will also read/write files under scripts/ and scripts/memory and create agent_data/chanjing_videos — scope includes other local skill paths and system state beyond the stated marketing analysis function.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no formal install spec (instruction-only), but SKILL.md tells users to git clone from GitHub. Cloning from the project's GitHub is expected for an open-source tool; however, the repo contains committed credential values and code that will invoke system binaries if present. No packaged install reduces supply-chain assurances.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The repo includes a committed scripts/config.js containing apparent API credentials (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY). The manifest claims config.js should be in doNotCommitToVcs (i.e., not committed), yet the file is present with keys — this is a serious inconsistency. The skill does not request environment variables but will use these keys and network access to external services. It also reads user environment (DISPLAY, DESKTOP_SESSION) and looks up ~/.openclaw-agent2 — accessing other user-specific paths.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good), but the code attempts to discover and execute another skill's script at ~/.openclaw-agent2/.../run_render.py (cmd_vid_integration.py). That means the skill can invoke or depend on other skills' code on the host. It also writes files under scripts/memory and agent_data (creates artifacts in the environment). The manifest says it does not modify other skills, but the code's behavior can reach into and execute other skills — a mismatch and potential privilege/containment concern.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
Key issues you should act on or consider before installing:

1) Do not run this code unmodified. The repo contains apparent API keys (scripts/config.js). Treat those keys as compromised: do not reuse them and consider rotating keys for any services you control.
2) The skill runs shell commands (execSync), may start Xvfb and expects /usr/bin/google-chrome. If you plan to run browser-mode scraping, only do so in a tightly sandboxed environment and verify the exact commands. The SKILL.md and manifest claim no extra binaries, but the code requires them.
3) The skill can call into other local skills (cmd_vid_integration.py looks up ~/.openclaw-agent2/... and will execute run_render.py). If you have other skills installed, this skill may invoke them — review and sandbox accordingly.
4) The manifest/network allowlist does not match runtime behavior (code scrapes douyin.com). Confirm and restrict network hosts before allowing outbound traffic.
5) Recommended remediation before use: remove committed secrets and require the user to supply keys at runtime (or use environment variables), update manifest to declare required binaries (chrome, Xvfb) and hosts, and audit/limit any code that executes external commands or other skill scripts.

If you don't have the ability to fully audit and sandbox this skill, avoid installing it or run it only in an isolated, disposable VM/container and rotate any keys that were exposed.
llm.findings:
[hardcoded_secret_in_config_js] unexpected: scripts/config.js contains literal-looking API credentials (TIKHUB_TOKEN and DEEPSEEK_KEY). A marketing analysis skill should request API keys or read them from a config, but committed keys are not appropriate and are not justified by the manifest/README. Manifest even lists config.js in doNotCommitToVcs, yet the file is present.
[child_process_execSync_and_shell_commands] expected: marketing_hub.js uses child_process.execSync to launch google-chrome and Xvfb for browser scraping. Browser automation can be legitimate for scraping data when documented, but the skill did not declare those binary requirements in metadata or SKILL.md (which claims only Node 18+). The use of execSync to run arbitrary shell commands increases execution risk.
[local_skill_invoke_path] unexpected: scripts/cmd_vid_integration.py references a path under ~/.openclaw-agent2/workspace-collector/skills/chanjing-one-click-video-creation/scripts/run_render.py and will attempt to execute it if present. Invoking another skill's script is not documented in the manifest and can lead to unexpected cross-skill execution.
[undocumented_network_targets] unexpected: Code performs browser scraping of douyin.com (chromeSearch builds douyin.com URLs), but manifest allowed_hosts/documentedHosts only list api.tikhub.io and api.deepseek.com. The skill's network use is broader than declared.
